description: Dependency updates through the Mend Renovate GitHub App: Terraform providers (constraints and the lock files of the roots), registry modules, the AWS ruleset of .tflint.hcl, the images pinned in the Makefile and the actions of .github/workflows/.

Every update is a pull request someone reads and merges by hand: no automerge. A provider or module update changes what the next apply does, so read its changelog first (a major of terraform-aws-modules/eks has breaking changes). A release is proposed only once it is 3 days old, because a hijacked release is usually pulled within hours (trivy, March 2026); vulnerability alerts skip that wait and the schedule.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Opened at once, outside the schedule and without minimumReleaseAge. Needs the repository's Dependency graph and Dependabot alerts.

customManagers.description: Images pinned as <image>:<tag>@sha256:<digest> with a '# renovate: datasource=docker depName=<image>' line right above (TERRAFORM_IMAGE, TFLINT_IMAGE, TRIVY_IMAGE, SHELLCHECK_IMAGE, ZIZMOR_IMAGE of the Makefile).

packageRules.description: chore(deps) for every update; vulnerabilityAlerts above turns a vulnerability fix into fix(deps).
GitHub Actions, pinned to a full commit SHA with the version in a comment: one pull request for non-major updates.
The images of the checks (Makefile): one pull request for non-major updates. TRIVY_IMAGE is also pinned in the code repository's Makefile: keep the two in step.
The Terraform of the dev machine runs plan and apply: a new TERRAFORM_IMAGE must stay inside required_version of every root, and the Homebrew Terraform follows it.
prBodyNotes: Upgrade the Terraform of the dev machine to the same version before the next plan, and check required_version of every root still allows it.

packageRules.description: A provider update rewrites the lock files of the roots: make check in CI uses them read-only, so a lock file without the hashes of linux_amd64 fails there (fix with make lock DIRS=<root>).
prBodyNotes: Run make lock DIRS=<root> for each changed root if CI reports missing hashes, and read the provider changelog before the next apply.
